_comment: Authored analysis: ownership, lifecycle, refcount and locking judgements that no composer can derive, keyed to the C entities they describe. The structural half of each record (field layout, signatures, footprints, casts) is composed from the CodeQL tables on demand and merged in at read time, so a re-extract rewrites nothing here. Written only by `crustify-oracle <target> query {types,symbols} --update`; read through crustify.manifests. Hand-edit at your own risk: `--update` validates a submission against the composed skeleton (unknown field, wrong kind, ptr-invariant violation) and this file does not.

ptr.note: AVAudioFifo owns the av_calloc-allocated table and every AVFifo element. av_audio_fifo_free releases each non-null element through av_fifo_freep2, then releases and nulls the table through av_freep. The field may be NULL during failed construction, and the table and FIFO contents are mutated by allocation, read/write, grow, drain, and reset operations. It is an array of owned pointers, with nb_buffers supplying its element count.

types.name: AVBuffer
types._comment_agent: AVBuffer is public only as an opaque identity behind AVBufferRef. Its internal data allocation is released by the stored callback at the last reference; opaque is runtime-polymorphic callback state and may either be transferred to that callback or borrowed until it runs; free is installed to a non-null static callback on construction. No independent AVBuffer storage dropper is valid because pool entries embed the object.

ptr.note: Byte array of size bytes. av_buffer_create transfers it to the AVBuffer; the stored free callback receives it when the last AVBufferRef is released.
Construction replaces NULL with av_buffer_default_free, so every initialized AVBuffer holds a static code pointer invoked at the last reference.

Type-erased callback state retained until free runs. The callback contract is runtime-polymorphic: callers may transfer context for the callback to dispose or retain externally owned state through the callback.

types.name: AVBufferRef
types._comment_agent: buffer_create initializes both pointers; av_buffer_ref copies the header and increments buffer->refcount; buffer_replace/av_buffer_unref free the reference header and release the underlying buffer on the last count. data is a borrowed window whose extent is size and whose storage lifetime is kept by buffer.

ptr.note: This AVBufferRef owns one reference-count unit to the underlying AVBuffer. av_buffer_unref drops that unit; AVBuffer internals including the atomic refcount are mutated through the pointer.

Points at a size-byte window into the allocation kept alive by buffer; references may select different subranges. It can be NULL for an empty/user-supplied zero-size buffer and is writable only under AVBuffer's public writability convention.

types.name: AVChannel
types._comment_agent: AVChannel is a by-value C enum with no pointer or lifecycle slots. The inclusive ambisonic endpoint range contains values without individual enumerators, so the Rust surface must remain integer-representable.

types.name: AVChannelCustom
types._comment_agent: The opaque field has no libavutil toucher. Custom maps are calloc'd, byte-copied by av_channel_layout_copy, and freed as arrays without per-element disposal, proving this cookie is borrowed and application-managed.

ptr.note: Application-owned, type-erased private data. libavutil never dereferences or frees it; av_channel_layout_copy copies the pointer value with the map, so the application must keep any pointee alive for every copied layout that retains it.

types.name: AVChannelLayout
types._comment_agent: The order field discriminates u. NATIVE and AMBISONIC use the mask; CUSTOM owns the map; UNSPEC leaves u undefined. The opaque cookie is external application state and survives libavutil layout copies by address only.

ptr.note: Application-managed type-erased cookie. Libavutil preserves and copies the address but never dereferences or frees it; its lifetime must cover every layout copy retaining it.
When order is CUSTOM, the layout owns an nb_channels-element AVChannelCustom array allocated by libavutil and released by av_channel_layout_uninit. Other union variants do not carry a live map.

types.name: AVChannelOrder
types._comment_agent: C enum has no pointer or lifecycle fields.

types.name: AVChromaLocation
types._comment_agent: C enum has no pointer or lifecycle fields.

types.name: AVDictionary
types._comment_agent: AVDictionary owns its elems array and the strings held by its inline entries; av_dict_free tears down that complete graph.

ptr.note: elems is the dictionary-owned growable array of count inline AVDictionaryEntry values. av_dict_set reallocates and writes it; an empty dictionary may hold NULL; av_dict_free releases every entry key/value and then the array.

types.name: AVDictionaryEntry
types._comment_agent: AVDictionaryEntry lives by value in AVDictionary.elems. It has no standalone public constructor or disposer; AVDictionary owns the entry array and disposes both owned strings. Public lookup/iteration returns borrowed entries whose fields remain valid only while the dictionary is unchanged.

ptr.note: Every live entry owns one av_malloc-family NUL-terminated key. av_dict_set rejects NULL or allocation failure before insertion; no observed path writes through a stored key pointer. The containing dictionary frees it, and published borrowed entries forbid caller mutation.

Every live entry owns one av_malloc-family NUL-terminated value; NULL requests deletion and is never inserted. AV_DICT_APPEND may realloc and write the stored value internally, while published borrowed entries forbid caller mutation. The containing dictionary frees it.

types.name: AVFrameSideData
types._comment_agent: AVFrameSideData headers are owned by a frame/side-data array rather than independently by public callers. The buf owner keeps the data window alive; metadata is a separate nullable owner.

ptr.note: A valid side-data entry owns one independently releasable AVBufferRef header. free_side_data_entry consumes it with av_buffer_unref; mutation of its bytes additionally requires av_buffer_is_writable.
A size-byte window into storage kept alive by buf, potentially at an interior offset. It is not independently freed; mutable access requires the backing AVBufferRef to be writable.
Optional dictionary owned by the side-data entry and consumed by av_dict_free when the entry is replaced or destroyed.

types.name: AVOption
types._comment_agent: AVOption is immutable persistent AVClass metadata and has no destructor, disposer, or cloner. Its string and array-definition pointers are nullable read-only borrows into static metadata; the default union discriminator is AVOption.type.

ptr.note: Active only when AV_OPT_TYPE_FLAG_ARRAY is set. It optionally points to one static const AVOptionArrayDef; all observed initializers are static and consumers only read it.

Active only for the string-encoded default option types (STRING, BINARY, DICT, IMAGE_SIZE, VIDEO_RATE, COLOR, CHLAYOUT). Source-tree option tables store a string literal or NULL; libavutil parses or copies but never frees this metadata pointer.
Optional read-only help metadata. All source-tree initializers use a string literal or NULL, and no lifecycle operation frees or replaces it.

AVClass option tables are persistent metadata arrays terminated by an AVOption whose name is NULL. Every definition in the source tree is static and names are string literals; libavutil only reads the NUL-terminated string.
Optional read-only logical-unit metadata. Initializers use string literals or NULL and libavutil only compares/logs the NUL-terminated string.

types.name: AVOptionArrayDef
types._comment_agent: AVOptionArrayDef has no lifecycle operation. Its def slot is nullable borrowed read-only static string metadata, not an av_malloc-family owner.

ptr.note: AVClass option is required to be a static AVOption array, and every AVOptionArrayDef initializer is static; its optional def is always a string literal. The struct never frees or mutates the NUL-terminated pointee, and consumers only read it through strlen/strcmp/logging.

av_free consumes an av_malloc-family allocation of any byte-level shape and releases its storage; NULL is explicitly allowed (documented in mem.h and forwarded unchanged). All three shapes are observed at the callsites: singletons (av_aes_ctr_free's a, av_encryption_info_free's info), counted buffers (executor_free's e->threads, av_encryption_info_free's info->subsamples, av_file_unmap's bufptr on a build without HAVE_MMAP), and NUL-terminated av_strdup/av_strndup strings (av_dict_set's copy_key/copy_value, parse_channel_list's chname). array is by_val, not by_ref, even where the buffer holds pointers (av_encryption_init_info_free's info->key_ids): the caller frees every element first, so av_free neither owns nor borrows the elements a by_ref block would have to describe -- to it the buffer is opaque bytes. mutable is null, not false: the body only forwards ptr to free, or to _aligned_free where HAVE_ALIGNED_MALLOC holds, and both are external symbols with no definition in this extraction, so no body inspection can decide whether the released block is written; it is not observably read-only either, since a real allocator writes its own bookkeeping into it. This matches the same-shape verdict already recorded on free, whose sole in-scope caller this is. The allocator family is a build-time property -- MALLOC_PREFIX renames free, and HAVE_ALIGNED_MALLOC swaps in _aligned_free -- so an av_free pointer must come from av_malloc/av_realloc and never from plain malloc.

av_md5_alloc returns NULL on allocation failure or transfers a fresh, writable AVMD5 allocation to the caller. Its sole operation is av_mallocz(sizeof(struct AVMD5)), so every byte is initialized to zero and the allocation belongs to the av_malloc family. In-tree owners in av_hash_alloc and av_hmac_alloc eventually release this context through av_free; the Rust AVMD5 CDropped implementation preserves that allocator match. The caller must still call av_md5_init before hashing: zero-filled storage is allocated and initialized as bytes, but does not yet contain the algorithm's initial state.

av_memdup reads size bytes from p as the memcpy SOURCE and neither stores, frees nor writes it: const in the type forces mutable=false, and the read does not outlive the call, so the borrow names its own arg. p==NULL short-circuits to a NULL return with no allocation, and opt_copy_elem depends on that -- it passes *src8, the possibly-unset payload of an AV_OPT_TYPE_BINARY option, and treats a NULL result as an error only when len is non-zero. Every shape observed in this extraction is multi-byte: a counted buffer of uint8_t* channel pointers (av_frame_ref, av_frame_replace: sizeof(*extended_data)*ch), a counted binary payload (opt_copy_elem: len read from the option's companion int), and a NUL-terminated string (av_bprint_finalize: real_size = FFMIN(buf->len+1, buf->size), which always spans the terminator, truncated or not). scalar stays by_val on the published mem.h contract -- av_memdup is exported as a general byte-copy primitive and in-tree callers outside this extraction duplicate single objects with it (libavcodec/pthread_frame.c av_memdup(avctx, sizeof(*avctx)), fftools/ffmpeg_dec.c av_memdup(subtitle, sizeof(*subtitle))) -- not on any libavutil callsite; the earlier note's claim of a libavutil singleton callsite was unsupported. array is by_val, not by_ref, even at the frame callsites whose elements are pointers: av_memdup copies bytes and never reads a pointee, so it neither owns nor borrows the elements a by_ref block would have to describe. Same verdict, same reason, as av_free's arg.

Returns a fresh av_malloc allocation of size bytes holding a byte-exact copy; ownership transfers to the caller and av_free -- the recorded dropper of this family, and the same AvFree strategy in the Rust wrapper -- releases it. NULL means p was NULL or the allocation failed; av_malloc fails on OOM and on any request above the av_max_alloc limit (INT_MAX by default), which is why every caller checks the return (opt_copy_elem only when its len is non-zero, since a zero-length binary option legitimately yields NULL from a NULL source). A zero size with a non-NULL p is NOT the NULL case: av_malloc(0) retries at one byte, so the caller still receives, and still owns, a live allocation. INITIALISATION EXTENT, and it is av_memdup's doing rather than the allocator's: for size>0 the block is exactly size bytes and the memcpy writes every one of them, so the whole allocation arrives initialised and a caller may immediately read it as size/sizeof(T) values of the element type it copied. A bare av_malloc return carries no such guarantee -- its only write is the optional CONFIG_MEMORY_POISONING memset, which this campaign's configuration compiles out -- so the two are not interchangeable as the source of a counted, typed owner even though both are released by the same av_free. The one uninitialised byte in this function's output is the size==0 retry byte, which memcpy does not reach; it is unobservable because the matching element count is zero, and it is why a zero-length result must not be re-counted as holding an element. The copy is shallow, which the shape records as by_val rather than by_ref: where the source holds pointers (av_frame_ref's extended_data) the result aliases the same pointees, kept alive by the frame's AVBufferRefs and not by this allocation. Alignment is av_malloc's ALIGN (64/32/16 by SIMD config), so the copy is re-castable to whatever element type the source held. string is true for the av_bprint_finalize path, whose copy carries the source terminator.

free consumes a malloc-family allocation; the allocation may hold a singleton, a counted byte/element buffer, or a NUL-terminated string, and NULL is accepted. mutable is null, not false: free is an external symbol with no definition in this extraction, so no body inspection can decide it -- and it is not observably read-only either, since a real allocator writes its own bookkeeping into the released block. Sole caller in scope is av_free, which forwards ptr unchanged and inherits the same shape. INITIALISATION EXTENT: free places NO initialisation requirement on the block. It releases storage and never reads a value out of it, so the scalar/array/string shapes above say what an allocation MAY hold, not what it DOES hold at the moment of release; that is why all three arms can share one dropper. The requirement lives on the OWNER instead, and this is where malloc and av_memdup part company: a bare malloc return is entirely unwritten -- unlike av_malloc it has not even a CONFIG_MEMORY_POISONING memset to point at -- so it does not yet hold count values of any element type, and a counted typed owner over it is invalid before any view is taken. Such a buffer must be adopted through an uninitialised tier and promoted once filled; only the erased singleton and the already-NUL-terminated string arms can adopt fresh storage as it stands. ZERO SIZE: malloc(0) is implementation-defined and may return NULL, which is indistinguishable from the OOM NULL and is rejected at the wrapper seam anyway; on this campaign's glibc it instead returns a unique live block, measured at 1 byte by LeakSanitizer. So a zero-length owner still owns storage and its release must NOT short-circuit on a zero byte length the way munmap's does -- a guard there leaks, demonstrated by injecting one and watching LSan report the byte. This differs from av_malloc only in mechanism (av_malloc explicitly retries at one byte, malloc's minimum block is the allocator's), not in consequence.

munmap consumes a whole mapped byte range; its separate size argument supplies the extent, so the pointer is array-shaped only and never a singleton or a string. Sole caller in scope is av_file_unmap, which returns early unless bufptr is non-null AND size is non-zero, so the range handed over is always a complete, non-empty MAP_PRIVATE mapping produced by av_file_map's mmap(NULL, size, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE, fd, 0); the release is page-granular, covering ceil(size/pagesize) bytes. mutable is null, not false: munmap is an external symbol with no definition in this extraction, so no body inspection can decide it.
